claim: Heston, Korajczyk and Sadka (JF 2010, arXiv 1005.3535): a stock return in a half-hour interval is positively related to its return in the same half-hour interval on each of the previous 40 trading days; the Day 1 decile long/short earns 3.01 bp per half-hour at the same time next day, over 11 bp in the opening half-hour and averaging 1.75 bp over the rest of the day.
quote: over 11 basis points in the opening half-hour
limitations: 2001-2005 sample; gross of costs (the paper compares 3 bp with a 1.7 bp half quoted spread for S&P 500 names); the arXiv snapshot was pdftotext of the full paper, tables were not re-derived here.
independent_replication: Haendler-Heston-Korajczyk-Sadka 2025 report the pattern persists out of sample.
impact_on_spec: Sets the magnitudes the two decision cells are compared against (open > 11 bp, close > 8 bp) and the same-period signal S_{X,L}.

claim: Haendler, Heston, Korajczyk and Sadka (2025, The Intra-Day Stock Return Periodicity Puzzle, abstract): the periodicity persists out of sample, is strongest at the open and close, and open periodicity is driven by VWAP trading while close periodicity is driven by market-on-close trading; VWAP-like trading explains part of the open and midday periodicity and up to 30 percent of the closing interval.
quote: open periodicity is driven by VWAP trading
limitations: Only the SMU repository abstract was read; the SSRN full text (abstract_id 5749704) returned 403 via curl and a captcha page via r.jina.ai (haendler_ssrn_jina.txt), so table magnitudes were not verified.
independent_replication: Consistent with Heston et al. 2010; no independent tradability study with auction costs.
impact_on_spec: Mechanism for using the opening auction entry and the closing auction exit; supports the decision-cell split into open and close.

claim: Lou, Polk and Skouras (JFE 2019): dollar trading volume is decomposed over 30-minute windows, the first window starting at 9:30 includes the opening auction and the last window includes the closing auction; overnight and intraday components of strategy returns are separated by these windows.
limitations: Read for the half-hour volume decomposition and definitions only, not for the C2a overnight claim (covered by t20260929_35_overnight_persistence).
independent_replication: Related decomposition in Akbas et al. 2022.
impact_on_spec: Defines the boundary windows (first and last half hour) used for r_O and r_C and shows that they contain the auctions.

claim: Bogousslavsky (JFE 2021): lending fees are typically charged only on positions held overnight, so arbitrageurs trading on mispricing reduce their positions before the end of the day; a mispricing factor earns positive returns throughout the day but performs poorly at the end of it.
quote: reduce their positions before the end of the day
limitations: Abstract-level snapshot; suggests the closing half-hour may carry a negative arbitrageur-flow component, which cuts against a same-period long/short in C.
impact_on_spec: Alternative explanation for a weak or reversed close-period edge; motivates the r_C1/r_C2 split.

claim: Goyal, Jegadeesh and Wu (JFQA 2026): price impact is lower in closing auctions than in the continuous market for all stocks except Nasdaq microcaps; opening auctions are illiquid (median opening auction volume about 0.92 percent of ADV).
quote: price impact is lower in closing auctions than in the continuous market
limitations: Opening auction illiquidity is a caution for the opening leg of the O decision cell; the 2 bp auction cost in the contract is an assumption, not measured here.
impact_on_spec: Supports the closing-auction exit at 2 bp and warns that the opening-auction entry is the more expensive leg.

claim: NYSE data insights: in Q2 2024 US closing auctions matched 55.5 bn dollars per day and accounted for 9.44 percent of total notional value traded, a record high.
limitations: Exchange marketing-style data note; supports the recent-strength argument for close-period flow only.
impact_on_spec: Recent-window motivation for C_L20_P1500 (closing flow share at a record).

claim: Alpaca orders documentation: OPG orders execute only in the opening auction and are rejected if submitted after 9:28am ET before 7pm; CLS orders are rejected if submitted after 3:50pm ET before 7pm and are routed to the primary exchange auctions.
quote: CLS orders submitted after 3:50pm but before 7:00pm ET will be rejected
limitations: Documentation, not a fill test; cls and opg fill reliability on the paper account is unmeasured.
impact_on_spec: Execution contract: opening-auction entry before 09:28 ET, closing-auction exit before 15:50 ET.

claim: Alpaca margin and short selling documentation: $0 locate and borrow fees on all easy-to-borrow shares for Trading API users; over 5,000 ETB securities.
quote: $0 locate and borrow fees on all ETB shares
limitations: The ETB list is not point in time in our data; the DTC quantile below 0.90 is the easy-to-borrow proxy for the short leg.
impact_on_spec: Short leg carries no borrow fee because positions are intraday only and restricted to the ETB proxy.

claim: Abdi and Ranaldo (RFS 2017): a bid-ask spread estimator built from daily close, high and low prices that outperforms the Corwin-Schultz high-low estimator and the Roll model for less liquid assets.
limitations: A daily estimate, not the half-hour quoted spread at 15:30 or 10:00; the marginal tier requires measured Alpaca quotes.
impact_on_spec: Supplies h = 0.5 x 21-day AR spread used for the continuous-auction leg cost.
